name: handler_filesize
title: Progression Handler: Progress Reported as the Size of a File on the File System

origin.description: Report progress by setting the size of a file to about the percent complete.
origin.usage: handler_filesize(file = "default.progress", intrusiveness = getOption("progressr.intrusiveness.file", 5), target = "file", enable = getOption("progressr.enable", TRUE), ...)

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path of the progress file. The default is "default.progress".

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is the option progressr.intrusiveness.file, or 5.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "file".

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If FALSE, the file is left untouched. The default is the option progressr.enable, or TRUE when that option is unset.

origin.details: On initiate, interrupt, and update, when the handler is enabled, the file size is round(100 * step / max_steps), or 100 when max_steps is 0. A size of 0 or an amount of 0 leaves the body unchanged. The body is "step/max: ", the message, padding dots, and " [percent%]", cut to that many bytes. finish removes the file when clear is TRUE and the file exists. Otherwise it writes the final size.
origin.example:
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".progress")
handler <- handler_filesize(file = path, enable = TRUE, clear = FALSE, intrusiveness = 0)
with_progress({
  p <- progressor(steps = 4, on_exit = FALSE)
  p(message = "work")
  p(message = "work")
  p(message = "work")
  p(message = "work")
}, handlers = handler, enable = TRUE, interval = 0, delay_terminal = FALSE, delay_stdout = FALSE, delay_conditions = character())
cat("handler_filesize wrote ", file.size(path), " bytes.\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Report progress by setting the size of a file to about the percent complete.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path of the progress file, or a text stream whose name is a path. The default is "default.progress".

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is the option progressr.intrusiveness.file, or 5.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "file".

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If False, the file is left untouched. The default is the option progressr.enable, or True when that option is unset.

arguments.name: extra
arguments.text: Further arguments passed to make_progression_handler(), including clear.

translation.details: On initiate, interrupt, and update, when the handler is enabled, the file size is round(100 * step / max_steps), or 100 when max_steps is 0. A size of 0 or an amount of 0 leaves the body unchanged. The body is "step/max: ", the message, padding dots, and " [percent%]", cut to that many bytes. finish removes the file when clear is true and file_test_f says the file exists. Otherwise it writes the final size.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile

from progressr.evaluate import with_progress
from progressr.progressor import progressor
from progressr.reporters import handler_filesize

path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "script.progress")
handler = handler_filesize(file=path, enable=True, clear=False, intrusiveness=0)

def body():
    progress = progressor(steps=4, on_exit=False)
    progress(message="work")
    progress(message="work")
    progress(message="work")
    progress(message="work")

with_progress(body, handlers=handler, enable=True, interval=0, delay_terminal=False, delay_stdout=False, delay_conditions=())
print(f"handler_filesize wrote {os.path.getsize(path)} bytes.")
